key_insight: Composition-tuned III-nitride monolayers show predicted thermoelectric ZT above 2.5 in selected p- and n-type cases, with n-type B₀.₂₅Ga₀.₇₅N exceeding 2 at 300 K.
engineering_relevance: These monolayers offer candidates for thermoelectric and high-field devices, with band alignments suggesting modulation-doping routes for both carrier types.
method: First-principles electronic structures and semiclassical transport for ordered BₓAl₁₋ₓN and BₓGa₁₋ₓN monolayers.
AMSET state-dependent relaxation times including acoustic deformation-potential and piezoelectric scattering.
Vacuum-referenced band alignments, explicit interface calculations, and a separate phenomenological breakdown-field model.
evidence_signal: Calculations predict approximately 1.6 × 10¹⁴ cm⁻² holes at an hGaN/V₂O₅ interface and breakdown fields of 20.06–20.74 MV/cm for the x = 0.75 alloys.
watch_item: ZT depends on the specified scattering model and fixed lattice thermal conductivity of 550 W/mK; breakdown estimates need monolayer validation and do not resolve field direction.
paper_title: Thermoelectric properties and modulation doping of ultrawide-bandgap nitride monolayers
